# CGRX v0.1.0-alpha.16

This prerelease improves the accuracy and explainability of code relationships without broadening the default language contract.

- Adds **opt-in** Swift exact-call evidence behind `experimental-swift`: uniquely resolved, unshadowed, zero-argument top-level free-function calls in one file. Ambiguous, member, imported and dynamic calls remain explicit gaps; Swift is not enabled by default.
- Makes C++ call extraction more conservative for shadowed and receiver calls, and reports unindexed working-tree changes as risk gaps instead of silently omitting them.
- Accepts the documented security-gate threshold and allowlist flags, while preserving strict validation of unsupported flags.
- Updates Cargo, npm and GitHub Actions dependencies, including the generated web bundles. The default graph and on-disk index format are unchanged.

The alpha.15 20,000-node / 120,000-relationship explorer remains available. JavaScript `.js` coverage and broader Swift CALLS, IMPORTS and REFERENCE proof are **not** claimed in this release; dynamic dispatch remains unresolved without binding evidence.

The Apple Silicon archive includes bundled web assets and `SHA256SUMS`. Linux and Intel macOS remain pinned source-install paths with Rust 1.89.0.
